t.4.62.1: With these and many other words, he who was skilled in speech praised me, took leave of me, and entered his own hermitage.
t.4.62.2: Creeping out slowly, slowly from a cave of the mountain, I climbed the Vindhya and now await you.
t.4.62.3: Today, more than a full hundred years have passed since that time; holding the sage's words in my heart, I am waiting for the right place and time.
t.4.62.4: But now that Niśākara has set out on the great departure and gone to heaven, anguish burns me, beset as I am by many doubts.
t.4.62.5: By the words of the sage I turn back my mind, which had risen toward death; and the resolve he gave me for the preservation of my life drives away my sorrow, as a blazing tongue of flame dispels the darkness.
t.4.62.6: And though I understood the might of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, I rebuked my son with harsh words: “How is it that Maithilī was not rescued?”
t.4.62.7: Though he heard her lamentation, and those two were left bereft of Sītā, my son did not do the kindness I would have wished, out of affection for Daśaratha.
t.4.62.8: Even as Saṃpāti was speaking thus with the monkeys, his two wings then sprouted forth before the very eyes of the forest-dwellers.
t.4.62.9: Seeing his own body adorned with newly sprung wings of reddish plumage, he felt incomparable joy and spoke these words to the monkeys.
t.4.62.10: Through the power of the great sage Niśākara, whose soul is boundless, my two wings, which had been scorched by the rays of the sun, have grown back again for me.
t.4.62.11: The valor that was mine when I was in my youth, that very same, along with strength and manly vigor, I perceive in myself today.
t.4.62.12: Let every effort be made by all means; you will find Sītā. This regaining of my wings is, for you, a sign that assures your success.
t.4.62.13: Having spoken thus to all those monkeys, Sampāti, the best of birds, flew up from the peak of the mountain, a sky-goer eager to know his power of flight.
t.4.62.14: Hearing those words of his, the tigers among monkeys, their hearts thrilled with delight, became eager for the triumph of their valour.
t.4.62.15: Then the foremost of the monkeys, equal to the wind in prowess and having regained their manly vigor, set out toward the direction facing Abhijit, eager to search for the daughter of Janaka.
